source_refs.note: Topic 2.9.1.2 Finally and Else (PDF 61, printed 58). The printed code is scrambled across columns; the lesson reconstructs it from the explanation. Flagged.

blocks.text: The finally block always executes, regardless of whether an exception was raised. The else block, if used, runs only if no exceptions were raised in the try block. These features are useful for ensuring certain code always runs and for executing additional logic when no errors occur.

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: In the printed book this listing is scrambled: pieces of several lines are set side by side in separate columns (for example "Ent er a", "number" and ""))" apart, and "f inally :" split). The code block above puts the printed pieces back in reading order.

The else block runs only if no exceptions are raised, and it displays the result of the division.  The finally block executes regardless of whether an exception occurred, ensuring that the completion message is printed.
